intended_object: For a commutative ring R and a matrix C ∈ M_n(R), the closed subgroup scheme of GL_n over Spec R that preserves C. Its points in an R-algebra A are {M ∈ GL_n(A) | M C Mᵀ = C}, and it is Spec of O(GL_n)/(entries of X C Xᵀ − C) (from the docstring and the module documentation, citing Milne 2.10).
explanation:
The body is `hopfSpec` applied to the quotient of the coordinate Hopf algebra of GL_n by `definingHopfIdeal R n C`. That Hopf ideal is the ideal generated by the entries of X C Xᵀ − C, where X is the generic invertible matrix and C is mapped into the coordinate ring through the structure map. The file proves the three Hopf-ideal closure conditions for these generators, so the quotient is a Hopf algebra. Its spectrum is an affine group scheme over R, and the file shows it embeds as a closed subgroup of GL_n.

The file also proves the points criterion `mem_definingPointsSubgroup_iff`: an A-point lies in the subgroup exactly when its matrix M satisfies M C Mᵀ = C. This is the standard definition of the group scheme preserving a bilinear form, using the row convention of Mathlib's `symplecticGroup`. The construction puts no conditions on C, so it covers every case, including n = 0 and the zero ring.

On generality: the base is an arbitrary commutative ring, which is the natural setting. Indexing by `Fin n` matches the library's GL_n, i.e. the standard GL_n, so it is not a real restriction. Mathlib has no group scheme of this kind; it only has the abstract groups `Matrix.orthogonalGroup` and `Matrix.symplecticGroup`, not schemes.
